text:
maya: FYI dedicated canary started showing p95 +200ms after yesterday's runtime merge, looks correlated with kernel selection changes. pausing rollout now :warning:
aj: thanks — can you paste the canary node IDs and a sample log?
sam: observed a big drop in KV cache hit rate on the canary hosts (~83% -> 61%), could explain extra token time.
perf-bot: profiler snapshot attached: hot loop is in kernel_selector.cpp:choose_best_kernel(), heavy time spent in heuristics when sequence_len distribution is bimodal.
perf-bot: top frames:
```
  1  kernel_selector.cpp:choose_best_kernel (41.7%)
  2  batch_scheduler.cpp:assign_batch (18.9%)
  3  kv_cache_manager.cpp:lookup_or_prefetch (12.3%)
```
liz: repro steps: checkout runtime@merge-9f1a, start dedicated-canary-42, run long-seq workload (mix of short/long requests) for 10k tokens, p95 spikes show up after ~5min.
maya: sample logs from one canary node:
```
[2026-03-17T22:03:12Z] kernel_selector: chosen kernel=matmul_radix32_quant (score=0.62)
[2026-03-17T22:03:12Z] kv_prefetch: miss key=ctx:abcd1234
[2026-03-17T22:03:12Z] batcher: formed batch size=48 latency=120ms
```
aj: weird — merge changed the batching hinting to favor larger batches for quantized kernels. That plus the changed kernel probe cost might be causing more cache churn and larger per-batch latency.
ken: I ran `kubectl logs canary-42 -n dedicated` and saw repeated kernel probe warnings and fallback to slow_path_kernel.
ken: snippet:
```
W kernel_probe: candidate 4 failing, falling back to slow_path_kernel
I kernel_selector: fallback path used 14x in last 60s
```
sam: also noticed prefetch window got widened in the merge, leading to more aggressive KV prefetch that thrashes eviction — hit rate drop matches that hypothesis.
maya: ops, what's the status of traffic? ops-bot: Canary rollout paused automatically at 42% due to latency policy. Routing: traffic shifted to stable pool and isolated canary nodes drained. No customer-facing reroute necessary yet but SLA risk if we continue.
ops-bot: Incident flag set: dedicated-canary-latency-2140304000. Pager duty oncall notified.
aj: proposed mitigations: 1) flip kernel-hinting flag to legacy (runtime.conf:kernel_hints=legacy) 2) revert the batching heuristic commit (PR #4821) 3) roll back the merge entirely if quick fix not found.
liz: I can put a quick feature-flag patch to disable widened prefetch window and run canary again.
ken: If we flip kernel_hints to legacy we should see immediate p95 improvement in staging perf tests — we tested that last week.
sam: bisect plan: narrow down between commits 9f1a..9f1d (kernel probe changes) and 9f1d..9f2b (prefetch widening). I'll start CI perf runs on both branches.
maya: decision: pause rollout (done), enable kernel_hints=legacy on canary nodes (aj), run targeted bisect (sam), prepare revert PR if bisect shows regression introduced inside kernel probe commit (liz). Owners: aj (ops), sam (bisect), liz (hotfix PR).
aj: executing flag flip now. running smoke tests.
aj: smoke tests: p95 back to baseline on one canary after flag flip (from 420ms -> 190ms). pushing change cluster-wide for canary group.
maya: thanks — keep this thread updated. if CI bisect reproduces we'll schedule revert hotpatch. :white_check_mark:
